niche.diet: grama_de_ceniza stems, rondo dung, meadow detritus

chains.trait: Six jointed legs and low, wide carapace
links: Stable footing required in tall grass and uneven litter
Low center of gravity prevents lateral tumbling
Dense air amplifies wind force per meter per second on exposed meadows

skill.effect: Hitches to grass stems, +40% survival in gales during the 26 h day/night cycle

chains.weakness: Stationary for 3 seconds, vulnerable to bite attacks
observe: Watch it lock its tarsi into grass blades when the breeze picks up.
Count six legs; the middle pair acts as stabilizers rather than climbers.
See its wide, flattened back catch the wind without rolling over.

journal.en: It doesn't fight the wind; it becomes part of the meadow.

plausibility.summary: A 3.2 cm, 0.4 g hexapod in tall meadow grass matches island detritivore size and the empty small-invertebrate decomposer niche (D28, D30). A low, wide body lowers the center of gravity on uneven litter; tarsal gripping on stems is standard for plant-dwelling Coleoptera. F19’s 1.6× wind loading matters most in exposed swards and during frontal gales; grass canopy shelters much of the litter layer, but open-patch anchoring still pays off.

analogues.organism: Broad-bodied scarab and tenebrionid dung/litter beetles (e.g. Scarabaeidae on pasture) that brace on substrate rather than resist wind in open air.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Acidic gut secretions and symbiotic rot-bacteria
links: Breaks down tough lignin and cellulose in dried grass and dung
Symbiotic microbes accelerate aerobic decay of organic matter
High partial pressure of oxygen fuels bacterial metabolism and spore turnover

skill.effect: Consumes detritus, converts to +15% local plant growth over 2 days

chains.weakness: Excretes nutrient-rich pellets that attract scavengers and mid-predators
observe: Notice the glistening secretion that softens dried stems on contact.
Watch pellets form in minutes, not days, as microbes digest.
See the faint bacterial shimmer in its translucent abdomen during feeding.

journal.en: A walking compost bin, turning yesterday's waste into tomorrow's grass.

plausibility.summary: Limit claims to bacterial-assisted digestion of dung fiber, softened grama_de_ceniza parenchyma, and engagement with pellet-surface fungi; drop explicit lignin breakdown or tie it to fungal hyphae ingested with detritus. Pellets attract scavengers—keep as honest ecological leak, not a bug.
fixes: Limit claims to bacterial-assisted digestion of dung fiber, softened grama_de_ceniza parenchyma, and engagement with pellet-surface fungi; drop explicit lignin breakdown or tie it to fungal hyphae ingested with detritus. Pellets attract scavengers—keep as honest ecological leak, not a bug.

analogues.organism: Dung beetle larvae and scarab gut microbiomes on herbivore feces; rove beetles (Staphylinidae) in decaying litter—cellulose-focused gut flora, not termite-grade lignin breakdown.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Fine tracheal network and spiracle valves
links: Extracts oxygen efficiently at low mass without massive body cavities
High pO₂ allows passive tracheal diffusion across short distances
Reduced spiracle size minimizes water loss in clear midday sun

skill.effect: Sprints 8m in 1.5s using stored tracheal pressure, +20% chase speed

chains.weakness: Valves seal in fog; loses burst capability and moves sluggishly in dense air/moisture
observe: Spot the tiny side openings that open and close rhythmically.
Observe rapid leg pumping before a sprint to flush the tracheal system.
Note it retreats under leaf litter when the valley fog rolls in.

journal.en: It breathes the thin air of the afternoon, but flees the heavy fog.

plausibility.summary: Rename O2-Burst to tidal spiracle flushing + short escape dash (~0.5–1.5 m/s for <1 s). Weakness in fog: cuticular wetting/cooling and lower meadow litter temperature, not spiracles sealing against hypoxia.
fixes: Rename O2-Burst to tidal spiracle flushing + short escape dash (~0.5–1.5 m/s for <1 s). Weakness in fog: cuticular wetting/cooling and lower meadow litter temperature, not spiracles sealing against hypoxia.

analogues.organism: Locust/schistocerca-style tidal tracheal ventilation (Weis-Fogh); dung beetles’ intermittent flight and short escape runs, not sustained cheetah-like sprints.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

chains.trait: Dark melanin-rich cuticle with UV-absorbing pigments
links: Shields internal tissues from seasonal UV pulses and photodamage
Dense air scatters blue light but concentrates ground-level UV in dry seasons
East-side meadows lack cloud cover to filter radiation during summer clearings

skill.effect: -30% radiation damage during midday, +10% camouflage on dark soil

chains.weakness: Absorbs heat; overheats during peak sun, forces midday shelter-seeking
observe: See its glossy black back shimmer and reflect harsh light.
Watch it retreat to grass shadows precisely at solar noon.
Notice how predator bites stick to its hard, dark shell without penetrating.

journal.en: It wears the sun's assault as armor, paying for it with heat.

plausibility.summary: Root Sun-Plated in heat–armor trade-off and bite resistance; keep modest UV benefit for clear summer midday, not F14 summit logic. Albino secret: fair—less heat stress at dawn fog (F8), higher desiccation/UV risk in open sun—still playable at 0.9× baseline UV.

secrets: Albino variant lacks melanin, thrives in cooler dawn fog but burns if caught in midday clear skies.
moments: When a herd of Rondos shifts, a sudden wind rolls through the grass, and thousands of them lock their legs, turning the meadow floor into a living, shimmering carpet that holds fast against the gale.

journal.en: It turns waste into wealth, one pellet at a time.
Under the yellow-white sun, black backs gleam like scattered beetles.
